newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel hopes to resume talks with Syria by January.
newsitem.headline: Israel hopes to resume talks with Syria by January.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Saturday he believed peace talks with Syria could be resumed by January.

"I am confident that we can restore the Syrian-Israeli peace talks soon, perhaps in January or maybe before, and we have committed ourselves to doing so," Netanyahu told the opening of an international business conference in Jerusalem.
Netanyahu said he was encouraged by statements on Saturday by Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara that Damascus would continue to seek peace with Israel.

After talks with French President Jacques Chirac in Paris, Shara said: "France would continue to cooperate with us (Syria) to push forward the peace process, to relaunch it and put it on the right track."

"There are a lot of declarations by Israeli leaders...these declarations are mainly positive, but the important thing is to translate them into actions, stick to the principles of the peace process and start where we left off," Shara said.

More than five years of talks between the countries have stalled over the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war. Damascus demands a full Israeli withdrawal while Netanyahu, who took office in June, has vowed never to return any of the strategic plateau.
Israeli-Syrian peace talks were suspended eight months ago after a wave of suicide attacks by Islamic militants killed 59 people in the Jewish state.
